messages.subject: Re: geom_jitter: is it allowed?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ron,

Thanks for taking your time to reply - it's such a helpful explanation.
I followed your suggestion and made an account in the RStudio community.

Thanks for being kind,
Nana

On Mon, May 30, 2022 at 3:27 PM Ron Crump <r.e....@warwick.ac.uk> wrote:
> Hi Nana,
>
> > I'm very new in R and currently learning geom_jitter. I've read many
> > sources about this geom but still can't understand how it is allowed to
> > add noise in your data.
> > pls_open.png
> >
> > For example, in these picture, OP explains that the bottom plot is using
> > geom_jitter thus avoiding overplotting. But from what I understand,
> > geom_jitter makes the plot changes the data point. In the geom_point,
> > there is no x 6,1 and y 20,1 but in geom_jitter there is.
> >
> > My question is: is it allowed?
>
> Yes.
>
> > Sorry if it sounds stupid, I learned basic statistic in college but
> > never about jitter.
>
> It isn't a statistical technique, it's a presentational one.
>
> Providing it is used with care - eg as in the example you presented
> with the jitter applied to number of cylinders - so that it gives an
> indication of the number of observations at each value of hwy, and does
> not infuence the variability in hwy, then it is fine. There are
> alternatives - you could colour each value based on the number
> of observations at that unique point, or vary the size. But often those
> would still overlap a lot.
>
> Regards,
> Ron.
>
> PS There isn't much traffic on this list these days, with
> community.rstudio.com <http://community.rstudio.com> being the preferred support forum for all
> things tidyverse-related, including ggplot2, so I'd recommend
> asking future questions over there.

messages.subject: Re: Increasing line size in color legend when using both color and size aesthetics?
messages.subject_clean: Increasing line size in color legend when using both color and size aesthetics?
messages.body_plain:
Hello! I know this is a pretty old thread, but I'm running into almost this exact issue and I haven't been able to find any solutions. In my ggplot2 plot, I've got three facets, each with its own color scheme (the default color scheme) rather than a continuation of colors, so each facet has red, blue, and green and each legend is labeled with the proper category (see below). This was accomplished with new_scale_color() after each "data = ~ subset(., filter)" geom_line layer. However, I'm publishing this content in a bookdown and when it's published, those tiny legend lines are almost non-existent.

I've tried using legend.key and using guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 50)) and neither work. Legend.key made the lines a little bigger, but not enough. If I remove the last new_scale_color(), override.aes does change the lines how I want, but only for the last legend. I need the lines bigger for all three legends.

Thank you,
Jason

messages.body_plain:
Dear Egbert,

> I need some help with a script for plotting daily rainfall map with isohyet

I recommend posing your question in the ggplot section of the
community.rstudio.com <http://community.rstudio.com> forums, as this list is not very active
these days.

And you will be much more likely to get a useful response if
you pose a specific question, with a reproducible example.
(Look at the guidelines on community.rstudio.com <http://community.rstudio.com> to see how
to create one, but code and example data are preferred).

Remember that the R community covers a broad
range of experiences, so most people will not know what
isohyet is, but with a well-posed question and reproducible
example that may not stop them from being able to help you.

Regards,
Ron.

messages.subject: Plotting points using different colors in ascending order using ggplot2
messages.subject_clean: Plotting points using different colors in ascending order using ggplot2
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I want to plot the species richness values of various plots on my map. However, I am struggling to apply different colours to the different points I have so far plotted. How can I get to color the points in the legend and on the map? See my seprodecable code. Attached is my current map and species richness csv file.  I would really appreciate any help on this.

library(ggplot2)
library(raster)
require("rgdal")
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(maptools)

Medicinal_richness<- read.csv("data/Preparing_all_data_2022/Prepared_richness/species_richness_tables/final_prepared_richness/thinned_medicinal_plants.csv", header = T, sep = ",", dec=".")

head(Medicinal_richness)
max(Medicinal_richness$Richness)
min(Medicinal_richness$Richness)

Kenya <- getData('GADM', country='Kenya', level=1) #Extracion de Peru
#Kenya_no_counties <- getData('GADM', country='Kenya', level=0) #Extracion de Peru
plot(Kenya)
class(Kenya)

Samburu_county <-Kenya[Kenya@data$NAME_1 == "Samburu",]
plot(Samburu_county)
Samburu_county_df<-fortify(Samburu_county)

plot2_best <- ggplot() + geom_polygon(data=Samburu_county_df, aes(long, lat, group = group), fill = NA, colour = "black") +  xlab("") + ylab("") + geom_point(data=Medicinal_richness, aes(x = long, y = lat, size=Richness)) + scale_size(name = "Total Richness", breaks=c(1,3,6,9,12,15,18), limits = c(2,18), labels=c("1-3 spp", "3-6 spp", "6-9 spp", "9-12 spp", "12-15 spp", "15-18 spp", "18-21 spp")) + theme(legend.position=c(.08,0.83)) ; plot2_best
